transformations.edit: Replaced the seed-only contract/body string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` argument and naming the return.

Attached the generated mutable array postconditions directly to the executable target: the `old(slice)@.len() == N` Some branch, old array-reference view, final-frame relation to `*final(ret.unwrap())`, and the None branch frame preservation.

Preserved the Rust 1.96 branch flow: `if self.len() == N`, then `as_mut_ptr`, pointer `cast_array`, unsafe mutable array-reference cast, `Some(me)`, and else `None`; the implicit receiver is the only source syntax adaptation.

Reused the already verified `core::slice::as_mut_ptr` dependency shape through a local executable `as_mut_ptr` wrapper with `slice_start_mut_ptr`, and isolated only Verus-unsupported `ptr.cast_array()` plus `unsafe { &mut *ptr }` as named source-backed raw-pointer/provenance and mutable array-reference final-frame boundaries.
